To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the wage behaviour of the firms and the unemployment rate are determined by the shape of the production technology, and that a convex (concave) production technology is associated with a competitive (collusive) wage behaviour and an unemployment rate that increases (decrease) together with the level of activity.

the shape of effort functions is crucial in determining the behaviour of firms in an efficiency-wage competition framework, as well as in determining the existence and the properties of the full employment equilibrium.

When workers are endowed with sigmoid effort functions, the symmetric Nash equilibrium of the economy is stable, full employment is associated with lower unemployment, and the wage behaviour of competitive firms follows a competitive pattern.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the consequences of the interaction of a large number of players in a market where the behaviour of the individual players is affected by the actions of the others.
the consequences of extending a competitive market structure to an economy in which workers are paid according to their effort.
the following question: What happens as the number of firms increases within a model of efficiency-wage competition?.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, as the number of firms increases, the wage behaviour changes from collusive to competitive and the labour exploitation changes from increasing to decreasing.
, in the presence of concave effort functions, efficiency-wage competition is a mechanism through which involuntary unemployment may emerge and persist.
the number of productive firms is not a crucial parameter to determine the existence of involuntary labour market equilibrium.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

, when the number of firms increases, the equilibrium is characterized by an unstable (stable) wage pattern, full employment is characterized (not characterized) by an increasing (decreasing) degree of labour exploitation, and unemployment is (not) a feature of the equilibrium.
the more competitive the environment, the more likely it is that workers will be exploited.
, when workers are more productive in the long-run than in the short-run, firms are able to sustain full employment.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the shape of an individual's effort function is crucial for the analysis of the efficiency-wage model and, more generally, for the understanding of the consequences of the interaction between firms and workers.
the number of players in an economy is a crucial determinant of the equilibrium allocation.
, in the presence of a concave effort function, the competitive outcome is characterized by a stable symmetric Nash equilibrium.
